original_question: Suppose (p1,N, ..., pℓ,N) is a good sequence of ℓ-tuples of real polynomials, meaning every nontrivial linear combination of the sequences p1,N, ..., pℓ,N is good in the sense that its exponential sums against every nonzero frequency tend to zero. Must it follow that for every ergodic system (X, X, µ, T) and f1, ..., fℓ ∈ L∞(µ), the averages (1/N) Σ T^[p1,N(n)] f1 · ... · T^[pℓ,N(n)] fℓ converge in L2(µ) to ∫f1 dµ · ... · ∫fℓ dµ?
target_in_paper: Section 5.1.2, Problem 10 (“Variable polynomials”). In this paper, the draft is aiming at the open problem asking whether a good sequence of ℓ-tuples of variable polynomials yields convergence of the corresponding multiple averages to the expected limit for a single ergodic transformation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the main mathematical content very well: it is about a single transformation T, ergodic systems, a good sequence of ℓ-tuples of variable polynomials, integer-part iterates, L∞ test functions, and L2-convergence to the product of the integrals. Those are exactly the ingredients of Problem 10 in Section 5.1.2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
missing_details: The paper’s setup is a sequence of one-variable real polynomials p_{i,N} indexed by N, and the family must have uniformly bounded degree; that bounded-degree hypothesis is part of the definition of a good sequence of polynomials and is missing from the draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
The ambient polynomial ring should be stated explicitly as R[t] (real-coefficient one-variable polynomials). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

For a single sequence (q_N), “good” means: for every nonzero real frequency α, the exponential sums (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N e(α q_N(n)) tend to 0 as N→∞; the paper uses this as the defining notion before Problem 10. The draft gives the idea but should state the quantifiers and the meaning of e(x)=exp(2πix) explicitly. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

For an ℓ-tuple sequence (p_{1,N},…,p_{ℓ,N}), the linear combinations should be specified as nontrivial real linear combinations Σ_i c_i p_{i,N} with fixed real coefficients c_i, not all zero. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
The floor notation [p_{i,N}(n)] should be identified explicitly as the integer-part function. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
The ergodic system should be written as (X, 𝓧, μ, T), with 𝓧 the σ-algebra; your draft has (X, X, μ, T), which is not stand-alone notation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
The quantifiers should explicitly say: for every ergodic system and every f_1,…,f_ℓ in L∞(μ), the averages converge in L2(μ) as N→∞. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should be presented as an open problem in the paper (“Show that …” / “Is it true that …?”), not as an already established theorem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
refined_question: Let (p_{1,N},…,p_{ℓ,N})_{N∈N} be a sequence of ℓ-tuples of real one-variable polynomials p_{i,N}∈R[t] of uniformly bounded degree. Call a sequence (q_N)_{N∈N} of real polynomials good if, for every nonzero α∈R, one has (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N e(α q_N(n)) → 0 as N→∞, where e(x)=exp(2πix). Call (p_{1,N},…,p_{ℓ,N}) good if every nonzero real linear combination Σ_{i=1}^ℓ c_i p_{i,N} is good. Is it true that, for every ergodic measure-preserving system (X, 𝓧, μ, T) and every f_1,…,f_ℓ∈L∞(μ), the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{[p_{1,N}(n)]}f_1 ··· T^{[p_{ℓ,N}(n)]}f_ℓ converge in L2(μ) to Π_{i=1}^ℓ ∫ f_i dμ, where [·] denotes the integer part? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in arXiv:1103.3808 because the paper first defines “good” variable polynomial sequences immediately before Problem 10 in Section 5.1.2 and then asks exactly for convergence of the corresponding multiple ergodic averages to the expected limit for every ergodic system. The draft is therefore targeting Problem 10, not the neighboring problems on characteristic factors or pointwise convergence. The nearby remark that the case ℓ=1 follows from the spectral theorem via identity (15) also matches the structure of your draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
